comparison: Perfect match on mutant analysis claims (C105, C110, C112, C113). Both evaluations support the MEK inhibition experiment as validation of the method's ability to detect phenotypic differences. OpenEval provides more technical detail about variance comparisons and scalogram interpretations, while peer review emphasizes implicit acceptance as part of overall method validation.

Perfect match on motivation claims (C2, C3, C10, C11, C115-C118) regarding limitations of traditional methods. Both evaluations support these claims as valid motivation. OpenEval notes these are based on general knowledge rather than systematic comparison, while peer review validates them implicitly through endorsement of the new method's advantages.

Strong overlap on level-set method validation (C33, C44, C47, C49-C53). Both evaluations support the methodology with quantitative validation data. OpenEval includes additional limitation claims (C125-C129) that peer review addresses separately in R9, noting methodological complexity. Both emphasize the method works well despite acknowledged approximations.

Strong overlap on strain rate computation claims (C54, C55, C59-C63, C130-C132). Both evaluations support the mathematical rigor and biological correspondence. OpenEval emphasizes mathematical citations and eigenvalue decomposition details, while peer review focuses on visual validation and acceptance of biological correspondence without critique.

OpenEval R3 addresses qualitative biological correspondence (C64-C68) that peer review R2 implicitly validates through acceptance of strain rate analysis. Both support the biological relevance, with OpenEval emphasizing Figure 2b visual evidence and peer review noting the method 'works well' through visual inspection.

Strong overlap on spherical harmonics analysis (C82-C84, C86, C87, C90). Both evaluations support the temporal patterns and biological interpretation. OpenEval provides detailed quantitative analysis of variance ratios and cell division connections, while peer review emphasizes unbiased identification of morphogenetic phases.

Strong overlap on wavelet analysis methodology (C91, C93, C142-C144). Both evaluations support the wavelet approach and its ability to identify developmental stages. OpenEval notes C145 as appropriate speculation about optimization, while peer review emphasizes the method's success in reflecting developmental stages without raising concerns.

Partial overlap on blastophore closure identification (C95-C97, C99, C100). Both evaluations support this novel finding. OpenEval emphasizes multiple lines of evidence (timing, topology, morphological patterns), while peer review R4 accepts wavelet results generally. Peer review R5 explicitly endorses blastophore closure as a novel sub-phase of gastrulation.

Partial overlap on two-step gastrulation mechanism (C102, C104, C38, C123). Both evaluations strongly support this finding. OpenEval emphasizes validation against prior work (Sherrard et al., 2010) and method validation, while peer review explicitly states authors 'obtain convincing evidence that ascidian gastrulation is a two-step process' as the central biological finding.

Partial overlap on overall capabilities and biological findings (C4-C6, C31, C32, C35-C37, C39, C40, C121, C122, C124). Both evaluations support the method's ability to identify known and novel processes. OpenEval provides comprehensive enumeration of capabilities, while peer review R5 focuses specifically on the two-step gastrulation finding as the key biological contribution.

Overlap on methodological advantages (C119, C120, C134, C135, C36). Both evaluations support automation and compression claims. OpenEval notes the 'unprecedented hands-off approach' may be overstated given parameter selection requirements, while peer review emphasizes quantitative analysis without segmentation/tracking as key advantages without raising concerns about the automation claim.

Partial overlap on spherical harmonics foundation (C72-C75) and its benefits (C133-C139). OpenEval R4 addresses mathematical foundation and acknowledges challenges, while peer review R3 focuses on biological interpretation and unbiased phase identification. Both support the approach, with OpenEval emphasizing honest acknowledgment of limitations strengthens credibility.

Minimal overlap on methodological challenges (C136, C139). OpenEval R4 notes these as honest acknowledgments that strengthen credibility, while peer review R9 addresses broader methodological complexity and accepts inherent limitations, noting the method's value will be understood as analyses accumulate.

Minimal overlap on limitations (C128, C129). OpenEval R1 notes these limitations strengthen credibility of validation claims, while peer review R9 addresses methodological complexity more broadly, with reviewers noting the mathematics is 'not straightforward to understand' but accepting the technical challenges.

OpenEval R13 addresses technical challenges motivating the level-set solution (C41-C43) based on continuum mechanics and biological reality. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; these claims represent problem statement rather than findings and are implicitly accepted through peer endorsement of the solution.

OpenEval R14 addresses speculative future applications (C146-C148) marked as uncertain due to lack of validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not comment on these forward-looking suggestions.

OpenEval R15 addresses extensive background and theoretical foundation claims (C1, C7-C30, C46, C72-C75, C91, C100, C114) that provide context through literature citations. No direct peer review evaluation of these background claims; peer reviewers implicitly accept the scientific context by focusing on novel methodological and biological contributions.
